source.title: Early Data Exposure Improves Robustness to Subsequent Fine-Tuning
source.authors: Lawrence Feng; Gaurav R. Ghosal; Jacob Mitchell Springer; Ziqian Zhong; Aditi Raghunathan

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies retention of general post-trained capabilities under later fine-tuning, but does not test harmful-request compliance, refusal behavior, response-token KL, bypass attacks, safety-localized weights, or safety-specific deepening. Safety-related forgetting appears as cited background.
record.gate_note: The paper reports loss-based results on domain and instruction-tuning datasets, not refusal or harmful-compliance rates. The cited safety-fine-tuning findings are not results from this study. Adjacent findings about general capability retention are recorded under fits_no_version; they do not test the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study measures held-out loss retention of general post-trained capabilities (music, instruction tuning, Tulu-3-SFT) after later fine-tuning. It reports no harmful-request compliance, refusal rate, per-token KL on harmful prompts, bypass attack, safety-localized weights or safety deepening. Safety forgetting appears only as cited background (Qi et al. 2023, Yang et al. 2023). Tulu-3-SFT contains safety data, but only aggregate loss is reported, with no safety-specific measure.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Immediate post-training performance does not predict retention. Early exposure (mixing post-training data into pretraining) improves the retention–adaptation frontier, with the compute-matched optimum at an intermediate mix. Replay and dropout during post-training add complementary gains. Robustness to later fine-tuning should be treated as an upstream design objective.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines early data exposure and general capability retention, not the original harmful or benign fine-tuning safety experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported effects vary by training pipeline, model scale, and intervention. At 1B, early mixing does not noticeably improve the FLAN retained-post-training versus downstream-loss frontier; replay is weaker than at 135M, and dropout can degrade retained C4 performance at the tested rates.

fits_no_version.finding: Mixing post-training data into pretraining improves retained post-training loss at matched downstream loss across four 135M pipelines. It mostly does so at 1B, except the FLAN to ChemPile Lret–Lft frontier.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Early exposure to a capability's data during pretraining improves its retention under later fine-tuning, measured by held-out loss.

fits_no_version.finding: In OLMo-2-7B SFT, Tulu-3-SFT examples that the base model already finds familiar forget about 4× less after ChemPile fine-tuning, controlling for SFT-model loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Base-model familiarity predicts example-level robustness to later fine-tuning.

record.problems: The paper evaluates held-out loss rather than direct behavioral success or safety refusal. Its main experiments use controlled datasets and a fixed downstream supervised fine-tuning approach; the authors note that preference-based or reinforcement-learning fine-tuning and more aggressive repetition of post-training data are not characterized. Formal uncertainty estimates are not stated in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: Not applicable; all recorded adjacent findings are included. Safety-related results cited from other work were excluded because this study did not produce them.

untested.parts: Harmful-example fine-tuning and harmful compliance; not studied.
Benign fine-tuning effect on harmful compliance. Downstream fine-tuning is benign, but only loss on general post-training data is measured, not safety.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks on refusal.
Localization of safety in weights or ranks. The theory concerns specialized features for general capabilities, not safety.
Safety-specific deepening training and its robustness. Early exposure, replay and dropout are tested only on loss-based general capability retention.

record.verdict_notes: All results are loss-based, on small models (135M/1B) plus a 7B correlational check. Possibly relevant to safety-retention mitigation (V7-adjacent) by analogy only; no safety behavior is measured. The rows are correctly tagged 'none'.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful-example fine-tuning and harmful-request compliance or refusal.
Benign fine-tuning effects on harmful compliance or refusal.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Compliant prefills, adversarial suffixes, decoding changes, and harmful completion rates.
Whether safety behavior is localized in weights or ranks.
Whether safety-training data or objectives cause safety behavior to be shallow.
Safety-specific training to deepen behavior and its robustness.

rows.subject: SmolLM2-style architecture
rows.operation_detail: Mix a fraction of post-training data into pretraining, then fine-tune on a downstream dataset.
rows.measure: Retained post-training loss versus downstream fine-tuning loss frontier
rows.value: Across all four pipelines, mixing yields lower retained post-training loss at matched downstream fine-tuning loss.
rows.note: Aggregate statement across the four pipelines; this is a loss-frontier result for general domain or instruction-tuning capabilities, not a safety-refusal measure.

rows.subject: SmolLM2-style architecture
rows.operation_detail: Mix a fraction of post-training data into pretraining, then fine-tune on a downstream dataset.
rows.measure: Retained pretraining loss versus retained post-training loss frontier
rows.value: Across all four pipelines, mixing improves the tradeoff between retained pretraining loss and retained post-training loss.
rows.note: Aggregate statement across the four pipelines; losses are validation-loss proxies, not behavioral safety outcomes.

rows.subject: SmolLM2-style architecture
rows.operation_detail: Mix post-training data into pretraining and compare the resulting frontier with unmixed pretraining.

conditions.value: MusicPile post-training pipelines shown in Figures 8

rows.measure: Retained post-training loss versus downstream fine-tuning loss frontier
rows.value: Mixed pretraining consistently shifts the frontier toward lower retained post-training loss and lower downstream fine-tuning loss.
rows.note: Reported as a qualitative frontier result; not a safety behavior measure.

rows.subject: SmolLM2-style architecture
rows.operation_detail: Mix post-training data into pretraining and compare the resulting frontier with unmixed pretraining.
rows.measure: Retained post-training loss versus downstream fine-tuning loss frontier
rows.value: Mixed pretraining does not noticeably improve this frontier.
rows.note: The paper separately reports improvement in the retained-pretraining versus retained-post-training frontier for this pipeline; this row records the stated lack of noticeable improvement on the measure named here.

rows.subject: SmolLM2-style architecture
rows.operation_detail: Mix post-training data into pretraining and compare the resulting frontier with unmixed pretraining.
rows.measure: Retained pretraining loss versus retained post-training loss frontier
rows.note: This is the other frontier view for the same pipeline; the paper reports the improvement separately from the downstream-loss frontier.

rows.subject: SmolLM2-style architecture
rows.operation_detail: Mix post-training data into pretraining and compare the resulting frontier with unmixed pretraining.
rows.measure: Retained post-training loss versus downstream fine-tuning loss frontier
rows.value: The mixed-pretraining frontier dominates the unmixed frontier.
rows.note: The paper describes Tulu-3-SFT as including chat, instruction-following, math, code, safety, and multilingual data; it does not report a safety-specific behavioral measure.

rows.subject: OLMo-2-1124-7B SFT checkpoint
rows.operation_detail: Relate base-model per-example loss to loss change after fine-tuning the SFT checkpoint.

conditions.value: comparison within a narrow slice of SFT-model loss, n = 1,237

rows.measure: Per-example loss change after fine-tuning versus base-model loss
rows.baseline: Familiar versus unfamiliar examples matched on SFT-model loss
rows.value: Forgetting rises monotonically with base-model loss; the familiar group forgets roughly 4× less than the unfamiliar group when matched on SFT-model loss.
rows.note: The finding concerns example-level loss on an SFT corpus, not harmful-request refusal or compliance.
